slides.title: Community and Environment
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 8 English, Unit 3: Community and Environment. In this unit you will explore how young people can make a real difference in their communities by protecting the environment. You will read two information texts about community action and about reading opinions closely, and the story "Rising Tide", about a girl named Imani who leads a youth movement called Coastal Rise to clean up a polluted bay in a coastal Kenyan city. Along the way you will master 31 vocabulary words and four grammar structures: clauses ending with prepositions, the second conditional, verb and adjective preposition pairs, and the present continuous passive. You will also learn the formal language of persuasion, such as "It is imperative that...", so that you can speak and write convincingly about the issues that matter to you. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Read and understand a complex narrative about community activism and environmental protection.
Use 31 new vocabulary words accurately in speaking and writing.
Construct clauses that end with prepositions naturally and correctly.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to read and understand a complex narrative about community activism and environmental protection. You will also use 31 new vocabulary words accurately in speaking and writing. You will also construct clauses that end with prepositions naturally and correctly. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: stifle, wane, commemorate, articulate, hasten, advocate. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: When a Community Decides to Act
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes When a Community Decides to Act and Three Voices from the Harbour. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Clauses Ending with Prepositions

slides.narration: The first language focus is Clauses Ending with Prepositions. In natural English it is perfectly correct to end a clause with a preposition: instead of the very formal "From which city did you come?", a confident speaker asks "Which city did you come from?", and the sentence loses none of its meaning. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Discussing the story. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use AI English for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
